text:
Priya: Heads-up — customer AcmeHealth opened a high-priority ticket: streaming responses for /v1/generate keep cutting mid-stream. They see a flurry of 502/5xx in our gateway metrics at the same minute and are being billed for partial streams. Ticket #CH-4829. Repro steps attached below from their side.

Priya: Logs they pasted:
```
2026-03-14T19:02:12Z gateway svc=gw-03 req=abcd1234 upstream=up-7 status=200 bytes=1024 conn_close=RST
2026-03-14T19:02:12Z gateway svc=gw-03 req=abcd1234 client_ip=1.2.3.4 downstream_close=RST counted_as=5xx
2026-03-14T19:02:12Z runtime svc=rt-1 req=abcd1234 model=redwood-13b stream_chunk=3/12
```

Priya: Customer says they did not cancel the request, they just saw the stream stop and then our endpoint returned 502. They attached a client-side log that shows TCP RST around the same time. They want a credit for billed tokens and a root cause.

Elliot: @Priya can you paste the trace link and the raw gateway log lines (with proxy codes)? also which region/cluster?

Priya: Region: us-west-2, cluster gw-03. Trace: <https://console.redwood/trace/tx-0a1b2c|tx-0a1b2c>. Customer sample curl used to stream (they used node); I converted to curl: 
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"prompt":"...long prompt...","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Jordan: Quick theory: we might be misclassifying downstream client-driven resets (RST/FIN) as gateway 5xx. If gateway sees a downstream reset after upstream sent partial chunks, our metric pipeline counts it as a 5xx. In reality the upstream served 200/partial and the client aborted. That would both: (a) show as an error spike in SRE dashboards, and (b) bill tokens if billing pipeline counts produced tokens before disconnect.

Jordan: Possible repro: run a streaming request and force a client RST (kill the curl process) after a few chunks. If the gateway counts that as a 5xx increase, we've reproduced.

Elliot: I'll query the logs for connection_close reasons and the gateway error classification. Running: 
```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM gateway_logs
WHERE cluster='gw-03' AND time >= now() - interval '1 hour'
AND req='abcd1234'
GROUP BY close_reason, status_code;
```

incident-bot: ALERT: spike detected: gateway 5xx rate +320% in us-west-2 (gw-03). Ticket #CH-4829 attached.

Nora: From billing POV we need to know exactly which requests/tokens were billed. Priya, can you confirm customer account id and the exact time window so we can do a potential refund if misbilled?

Priya: Customer account: acct-acme-098. Window: 2026-03-14 19:02:00 - 19:05:00 UTC. They provided request IDs: abcd1234, abcd5678, abcd9aaa.

Elliot: Quick follow-up after a first pass: majority of the events in that window show downstream_close=RST and upstream_status=200 or upstream_fragment_sent but gateway status mapped to 502. The mapping happens in the gateway policy where downstream resets are currently flagged as errors.

Elliot: Relevant snippet from gateway code that maps errors: 
```go
// in gateway/handler.go
if downstreamClosed && !upstreamError {
    // historically counted as 5xx to surface reliability
    metrics.Count("gateway.5xx")
    return 502
}
```

Jordan: That mapping is overzealous for streaming workloads. For long-lived chunks we should differentiate client aborts (RST from client IP within 2s of last chunk) vs actual upstream failures (upstream returned 5xx or connection error).

Jordan: Proposed immediate mitigation: change counting rule so we don't increment gateway.5xx for downstream RST when upstream_status==200 and at least one chunk was delivered. Also add a label `client_abort=true` to such events so billing can exclude them. This is conservative and reversible.

Nora: Can you confirm billing pipeline can filter on `client_abort=true`? We need minimal changes because accounting is sensitive.

Jordan: Yes — billing uni pipeline already consumes gateway events and respects optional boolean labels. We can add a transient label and rerun aggregation. Requires a small routing change and a short deploy to gw-03.

Priya: Customer is pushing for a credit today if misbilling is confirmed. Any ETA on a quick fix?

Elliot: I can test a config flip in gw-staging now and run a controlled repro. If results look good, we can roll to gw-03 within 45 minutes. I'll summarize counts before/after.

Elliot: Quick test results (staging): client kill after 3 chunks -> gateway metric NOT incremented, billing event labeled `client_abort=true`. Logs: 
```
2026-03-14T20:10:12Z gw-staging req=test123 upstream=200 chunks=3 downstream_close=RST client_abort=true
```

Elliot: Note: we still return 502 to the client in some clients due to the handler return behavior. Jordan will adjust the handler to return a 499-style semantic (client closed) but need to coordinate with SDKs.

Jordan: Patch in PR: https://stash/redwood/gateway/pull/452. Main changes: (1) metrics rule (2) emit client_abort label (3) map downstream RST -> 499 instead of 502 when upstream_ok==true.

tickets-bot: PR linked to CH-4829 and queued for canary.

Nora: If we flip metrics and run a backfill of the last 24h, we can produce a list of affected requests and propose credits. I'll wait for Elliot's validated lists.

Priya: Thanks. I'll message the customer with an interim update: "we're investigating, potential misclassification discovered, will update in ~1h and propose credits if applicable".

Elliot: Post-deploy update: canary on gw-03 rolled to 10% -> no odd regressions. Full roll scheduled in 30m. Preliminary numbers: of 2,340 gateway 5xx events in the window, ~1,050 were downstream RST with upstream_ok. Those would have been reclassified.

Elliot: Created internal ticket INF-9207 to backfill metrics and generate affected-request CSV for billing.

Priya: Great. Assigning CH-4829 -> Priya for customer comms, tagging INF-9207 for engineering. Nora, will you own credits once list is ready?

Nora: Yes, I'll prepare an offer and run it by finance.

Priya: Closing the loop here once INF-9207 delivers the CSV. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
